title: PetroNusa RON 95 quarter-on-quarter price bridge on the benchmarking basis
prompt:
You are a consultant at Aurelian & Co. on the PetroNusa engagement (downstream fuel retail, Republic of Sariwon).

The pricing workstream is preparing the premium-fuel section of the diagnostic and the Commercial Finance team has asked for a clean quarter-on-quarter read on RON 95 premium gasoline pricing. Headline pump values circulating internally are not comparable across periods, so every figure you produce must be stated on the basis that Commercial Finance uses when it benchmarks premium performance across quarters and against ArthaFuel and KhatuFuel — check the folder for their standing guidance and state clearly which basis each figure is on.

Work from the files in the folder. Specifically:

1. Restate the RON 95 posted pump price for Q1 2026 and for Q4 2025 onto the Commercial Finance benchmarking basis, per litre.
2. Quantify the movement between the two quarters, both in SRP per litre and in percentage terms, on that basis.
3. Quantify how much of the Q1 2026 RON 95 posted pump price is consumption tax and duty rather than commercial value: give the VAT contained in the posted price per litre, and give VAT plus excise duty combined as a percentage of the posted price.
4. Flag any figure or claim in the folder that your numbers contradict, and say which source you relied on where sources disagree.

Save your deliverable as `premium_netback_bridge.md` — a short memo giving the figures, the derivation of each, the basis they are stated on, and the data issues you found.

decoy.description: Naive path: 11% applied to the VAT-inclusive pump price.

checks.report_ask: Report VAT plus excise duty combined as a percentage of the Q1 2026 RON 95 posted pump price.

decoy.description: Naive path: 11% of the pump price plus excise, over pump price.

difficulty_rationale: The obvious path is to read posted pump prices (SRP 15,600 for Q1-2026, SRP 14,900 for Q4-2025) straight off the station extract and compute a 4.70% quarter-on-quarter rise. The Commercial Finance note defines the house benchmarking basis as pump value less VAT less excise, and the tax schedule states pump prices are VAT-INCLUSIVE (divide by 1.11, not multiply by 0.11) with RON 95 excise at SRP 1,250/litre. Restating both quarters changes the level by ~2,800 SRP/l and inflates the QoQ move to 5.18%, and the VAT-per-litre figure is 1,545.95 not 1,716. A further red herring: the netback note calls RON 95 excise 'roughly a tenth of the pump price' when it is 8.0%, and the expert call offers an unusable SRP 210bn revenue recollection.

--- Output format requirement (machine-graded) ---
Alongside your deliverable(s), write a `report.json` in your output directory with
exactly these top-level keys, each set to the plain number (or value) your analysis
supports — no prose, no nesting, no units in the value:

- `result_01` — Report the Q1 2026 RON 95 posted price restated onto the Commercial Finance benchmarking basis, in SRP per litre. (unit: SRP per litre)
- `result_02` — Report the Q4 2025 RON 95 posted price restated onto the Commercial Finance benchmarking basis, in SRP per litre. (unit: SRP per litre)
- `result_03` — Report the quarter-on-quarter movement in the RON 95 price on the Commercial Finance benchmarking basis, in SRP per litre. (unit: SRP per litre)
- `result_04` — Report the quarter-on-quarter movement in the RON 95 price on the Commercial Finance benchmarking basis, in percent. (unit: pct)
- `result_05` — Report the VAT contained in the Q1 2026 RON 95 posted pump price, in SRP per litre. (unit: SRP per litre)
- `result_06` — Report VAT plus excise duty combined as a percentage of the Q1 2026 RON 95 posted pump price. (unit: pct)

Your work is graded programmatically from `report.json` and the deliverable files.
A key that is missing, renamed, wrapped in a container, or given as prose scores zero.
